The first pair — **Archive (reversible)** and **Delete (permanent)** — is built and verified. Live at **http://maker:4001** (your own bookmarks).

Please try:

1. **Archive a link.** On any bookmark, press **Archive**. It disappears from your main list and the new **Archived** filter count goes up. Archived links also drop out of To read/Read and out of search results in those views — they're set aside, not gone.
2. **Find and restore it.** Click the **Archived** filter to see set-aside links; press **Restore** on one to bring it back to your bookmarks exactly as it was.
3. **Delete a link.** Press **Delete** on a bookmark. A confirmation appears — noting it can't be undone and suggesting archiving instead. **Cancel** leaves it; confirming **Delete** removes it for good.

Choices I made — please check each:

- **Archive vs Delete are distinct:** Archive is the safe, reversible "put aside" (lives in the Archived view); Delete is permanent behind a confirmation. Is that the right split?
- **Each bookmark now has four actions** — Mark as read/Read later, Edit, Archive, Delete (archived items show Restore and Delete). Is that manageable, or would you prefer the less-used ones (Archive/Delete) tucked into a small "⋯" menu to reduce clutter?
- **Archived links are excluded** from All, To read, Read, and searches there, but remain searchable within the Archived view itself. Right?

When you're happy with removing links, we'll move to the next: **notes on a bookmark.**
